why: Each figure is a hexagon with four parts: top, left, right and bottom, each with a V-shaped line and a dot. Going left to right, one V-line is removed each step in this order: right, top, left. So the next step removes the bottom V-line and leaves no V-lines. The dots go away one at a time too: the right dot first, then the top dot, then the left dot. So the bottom dot is the only thing left. Option 1 shows exactly that. Option 3 fails because it still keeps a V-line at the bottom.
trick: Follow each kind of mark separately (V-lines, then dots). Find the order in which each one disappears, then apply the next step to both.
note: Dots: all 4, 4, 3 (right gone), 2 (top gone), so next 1 (left gone). V-lines: 4,3,2,1 then 0.
